title: Formspec Respondent Ledger Event
description: A single append-only respondent-side audit event for the optional Respondent Ledger add-on. Events capture material draft, submission, correction, amendment, attachment, prepopulation, validation, and optional field-level edit milestones without redefining a Formspec Response as an event stream.

eventId.description: Unique identifier for this event within the ledger.

sequence.description: Monotonic sequence number within the ledger.

occurredAt.description: When the underlying material action occurred.

recordedAt.description: When the processor durably recorded the event.

responseId.description: Identifier of the Formspec Response this event belongs to.

definitionUrl.description: Canonical URL of the pinned Definition in force for this event.

definitionVersion.description: Exact pinned Definition version in force for this event.

authoredBy.description: Authoring identity for the actor that issued this event per ADR 0150 §5.4. Distinct from envelope `actor` (respondent-identity): `actor` answers 'in what respondent context did this event happen?' (local Actor $def, kind: respondent|delegate|system|support-agent|unknown); `authoredBy` answers 'who issued the authoring op?' (common AuthorActor $def, kind: human|ai-agent|service, actChannel: human|mcp|agent|service). REQUIRED when eventType matches `^(ai\.|user\.)`; optional otherwise. Module-contributed authoring events MAY layer their own require-rule via E603 lint / module contracts.

changes.description: Ordered set of atomic material changes associated with this event.

priorAttachmentBindingHash.description: Prior attachment-binding event hash referenced by an attachment.removed event.

recordKind.description: Correction-profile discriminator. Present only for response.correction-recorded events.

data.description: Structured payload for event types that define an event-specific data block.

sessionRef.description: Implementation-specific identifier for the respondent session segment associated with the event.

amendmentRef.description: Identifier for the amendment cycle this event belongs to, when applicable.

priorEventHash.description: Previous event hash in the respondent-ledger chain, or null for the first event in a Trellis-wrapped chain.

then.description: ADR 0150 §5.4: authoring events (eventType matching `^(ai\.|user\.)`) MUST carry envelope-level `authoredBy: AuthorActor`. Module-contributed authoring events under the `^x-` extension space MAY layer their own require-rule via module contracts or E603 lint.

oneOf.description: Module-contributed event type per ADR 0150 §4.5/§4.9. Lint E603 enforces module-declaration resolution.

Authoring-namespace event type per ADR 0150 §5.4/§8.5. The `x-formspec-ai-runtime` module ships nine baseline `ai.*` values (ai.command-issued, ai.command-completed, ai.command-failed, ai.suggestion-offered, ai.suggestion-accepted, ai.suggestion-rejected, ai.proposal-opened, ai.proposal-closed, ai.proposal-accepted); product MCPs contribute additional `ai.*` values through their declared module. `user.*` covers human-issued authoring acts. Events under this lane MUST carry envelope-level `authoredBy: AuthorActor` (enforced by the if/then at schema root). Lint E603 resolves the specific value against the document's declared modules.

EventType.description: Canonical event classifications defined by the Respondent Ledger add-on OR an `x-` module-contributed extension (ADR 0150 §4.5) OR an `ai.*` / `user.*` authoring-namespace event (ADR 0150 §5.4/§8.5). The first thirteen closed-core values are required event types; the remaining closed-core values are optional but standardized extension points — including the optional action.* kinds in §8.5 which record Response Actions invocation lifecycle when a processor implements the Response Actions companion (specs/response-actions/response-actions-spec.md §6). Extension event types follow the canonical `^x-[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z][a-z0-9]*)*$` regex (§4.8). Authoring events follow `^(ai|user)\.[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z][a-z0-9]*)*$` and MUST carry `authoredBy: AuthorActor`.

kind.description: Who initiated or is attributed with the event.

display.description: Human-readable actor label for timeline and support views.

assuranceLevel.description: Ordered assurance level per spec §6.6.1. Implementations MAY define additional levels; the base four are enumerated here.

identityProviderRef.description: Reference to the normalized identity provider, verifier, or adapter used for this actor context.

subjectRef.description: Stable pseudonymous subject or continuity identifier used by the ledger independent of any specific identity provider or proofing implementation.

kind.description: Capture channel or subsystem that produced the event.

deviceId.description: Stable or session-local device identifier when tracked.

ipAddressRef.description: Protected derivative or reference for network address metadata.

userAgentRef.description: Protected derivative or reference for user-agent metadata.

op.description: Atomic operation represented by this material change entry.

path.description: Logical Formspec response path identifying the changed node.

valueClass.description: Origin class of the changed value: closed-core (user-input, prepopulated, calculated, imported, attachment, system-derived, migration-derived) OR an `x-` module-contributed extension (ADR 0150 §4.5).

itemKey.description: Stable Formspec item key when the path maps directly to one.

accessClass.description: Resolved accessControl.class for the changed response field when a Privacy Profile or class-aware processor can resolve it.

before.description: Prior value when retained under the implementation's privacy policy.

after.description: Resulting value when retained under the implementation's privacy policy.

displayBefore.description: Human-readable prior value summary safe for timeline display.

displayAfter.description: Human-readable resulting value summary safe for timeline display.

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable explanation for why the change happened.

editBatchId.description: Identifier shared by ChangeSetEntry objects produced by the same durable save, coalesced autosave, submit attempt, amendment, migration, or merge-resolution boundary.

editSequence.description: Stable ordering index within an edit batch.

dataPointer.description: Optional JSON Pointer or equivalent row discriminator for precise targeting in repeated structures.

correctionTargetEventHash.description: Hash of the prior response-submission event being corrected.

correctedFieldSet.description: Declared subset of response fields corrected by this event. Each entry is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the prior submitted response.

fieldValues.description: Original/corrected value pairs preserved for verifier correction-preservation reports. Each path MUST appear in correctedFieldSet.

reason.description: Respondent-visible explanation of why the correction was recorded.

authorizationRef.description: Reference to the authorizing act that permitted the correction. This may be an algorithm-prefixed hash, URI, or implementation-local reference; the Respondent Ledger records the reference without owning workflow governance semantics.

path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer for the corrected field.

originalValue.description: Original submitted value, or a policy-safe representation when raw value retention is not permitted.

correctedValue.description: Corrected value, or a policy-safe representation when raw value retention is not permitted.

provider.description: Provider or issuer identifier, such as idme, login.gov, an internal proofing service, or a DID issuer.

adapter.description: Implementation adapter/interface identifier used to normalize a provider-specific identity flow into the canonical ledger shape.

subjectRef.description: Stable pseudonymous subject or continuity identifier bound to this attestation without requiring disclosure of a real-world identity in the ledger itself.

verificationMethod.description: DID URL, key identifier, or equivalent verification-method reference used to validate the attestation.

credentialType.description: High-level credential or attestation category captured by the event.

credentialRef.description: Reference to an encrypted token, credential, presentation, or provider-response envelope rather than the raw secret itself.

personhoodCheck.description: Outcome of proof-of-personhood, liveness, or uniqueness checks when applicable.

subjectBinding.description: Which party in the workflow the attestation is about.

assuranceLevel.description: Ordered assurance level per spec §6.6.1. Implementations MAY define additional levels; the base four are enumerated here.

selectiveDisclosureProfile.description: Named policy profile controlling what portions of the attestation may be revealed in support, review, export, or dispute contexts.

evidenceRef.description: Reference to encrypted reveal material, redacted export evidence, or provider-response evidence.

attesterTier.description: FW-0036 attester tier that produced the verdict.

attesterId.description: Opaque URN or adapter identifier naming the attester that produced the verdict.

outcome.description: Provider-neutral result of the bot-protection gate.

evaluatedAt.description: When the attester verdict was evaluated.

evidenceRef.description: Optional opaque attester-side audit reference. This field MUST NOT contain IP addresses, User-Agent strings, device fingerprints, geolocation, behavioral biometrics, or other re-identifying signals.

ResponseDeclinedData.description: Payload for response.declined. Records that the respondent affirmatively refused to complete or sign the form. Distinct from response.stopped (abandonment without affirmative refusal). Distinct from consent.revoked (revocation of a previously-granted scoped consent rather than refusal of the form act).

reason.description: Respondent-visible rationale for declining. Implementations honoring per-field accessControl.class SHOULD treat this as respondent-authored free text under the deployment's prevailing class for narrative reasons.

clauseReferences.description: Optional references to specific Definition clauses or disclosures the respondent objected to. Each entry is an opaque implementation reference (RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, item key, clause id, or disclosure id).

partyRef.description: Optional party scope for multi-party drafts (FW-0050 composition). Single-party flows omit this field.

ResponseWithdrawnData.description: Payload for response.withdrawn. Records that the respondent retracted a previously-submitted response. Pre-determination withdrawals are applicant-authoritative; post-determination withdrawals carry rescissionRequested=true and the issuer separately decides whether to emit the kernel rescission event (issuer authority, not respondent). Distinct from response.amendment-opened (cooperative re-edit) and response.dispute-attached (counter-attestation without retraction).

withdrawnAt.description: When the respondent issued the withdrawal.

reason.description: Respondent-visible rationale for withdrawal. Free text; class inheritance follows the same rule as response.declined.reason.

rescissionRequested.description: True when the withdrawal targets a determination-issued submission and requests rescission. The Respondent Ledger records the request; whether the issuer accepts and emits a kernel rescission event is governed elsewhere (WOS Kernel §13.9 amendment taxonomy when WOS is the governance layer).

withdrawalTargetEventHash.description: Hash of the prior response-submission event being withdrawn. Required when integrity chaining is enabled and the prior event is identifiable; omitted only when the ledger has no integrityProfile chain.

partyRef.description: Optional party scope for multi-party drafts (FW-0050 composition).

ResponseDisputeAttachedData.description: Payload for response.dispute-attached. Records a counter-attestation attached to a prior submission without retracting it. Dispute is a parallel record, not a lifecycle transition: the original submission remains in force, and the dispute is preserved alongside for verifier surfacing.

statement.description: Respondent-authored counter-attestation text. Free text; class inheritance follows accessControl.class on the deployment's prevailing class for narrative dispute statements (FW-0049 safe-* composition applies).

disputeTargetEventHash.description: Hash of the prior response-submission event the dispute targets.

disputedFieldSet.description: Optional narrowed field set the dispute speaks to. Each entry is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the prior submitted response. Omission means the dispute is response-scoped, not field-scoped.

partyRef.description: Optional party scope for multi-party drafts (FW-0050 composition). Dispute is signer-scoped by default in multi-party flows.

ConsentRevokedData.description: Payload for consent.revoked. Records that the respondent withdrew a previously-granted scoped consent (data-use, contact, downstream-disclosure, etc.). Aligns with GDPR Article 7(3) consent-withdrawal semantics. Distinct from response.declined (refusal of the form act itself) and response.withdrawn (retraction of a submitted response).

consentScope.description: Opaque identifier naming the consent scope being revoked. Implementations using a controlled vocabulary (e.g., W3C DPV dpv:Purpose tokens, Kantara Consent Receipt purpose ids) SHOULD use that vocabulary; ad-hoc deployments MAY use a deployment-local token.

consentGrantRef.description: Optional reference to the prior consent-grant fact being revoked (an algorithm-prefixed hash, URI, or implementation-local handle). The Respondent Ledger does not own consent grant authoring.

partyRef.description: Optional party scope for multi-party drafts (FW-0050 composition).

DataErasedData.description: Payload for data.erased. Records that the issuer durably erased a subset of respondent data and issued an erasure receipt. The ledger event is the respondent-side audit fact; the cryptographic erasure attestation lives in the Deletion Receipt sidecar (SC-2). Aligns with GDPR Article 17 right-to-erasure semantics.

erasedAt.description: When the issuer durably erased the data.

classesErased.description: Resolved accessControl.class tokens whose data was erased. Each entry MUST be a non-empty string drawn from the deployment's Access-Class Registry.

retentionWaived.description: Optional list of retention-policy identifiers waived for this erasure (e.g., legal-hold exceptions consumed). Empty or omitted when no retention waiver applies.

cryptographicMethod.description: Optional erasure method identifier (e.g., 'key-shred-x25519', 'overwrite-3pass', 'tombstone-with-anchor'). Opaque to the ledger; the Deletion Receipt sidecar owns method semantics.

deletionReceiptRef.description: Reference to the corresponding Deletion Receipt (an algorithm-prefixed hash, URI, or implementation-local handle). The ledger event MUST NOT substitute for the receipt itself.

DisclosurePresentedData.description: Payload for disclosure.presented. Records that a specific disclosure (privacy notice, consequence statement, plain-language summary, jurisdictional warning, AI-authorship banner) was rendered to the respondent at a specific point in the flow. Aligns with informed-consent receipt patterns (Kantara Consent Receipt v1.1).

presentedAt.description: When the disclosure was rendered to the respondent.

disclosureId.description: Stable identifier for the disclosure within the Definition or deployment registry.

disclosureHash.description: Hash of the exact disclosure bytes shown. Required so the verifier can prove that this specific disclosure version was presented even when the upstream content evolves.

displayContextRef.description: Optional reference to the surface/context where the disclosure was rendered (e.g., 'submit-gate', 'item:income_section', 'identity-step').

acknowledged.description: Optional flag indicating that the respondent acknowledged the disclosure via an affirmative-action gate. Absence does NOT imply non-acknowledgement; deployments that distinguish passive presentation from affirmative acknowledgement SHOULD populate this field.

FieldFlaggedByRespondentData.description: Payload for field.flagged-by-respondent. Records that the respondent self-flagged a specific field as uncertain, declined-to-answer, needing-review, or incorrect-as-prefilled. This is a respondent-authored audit affordance, distinct from validation findings (which are produced by the engine, not the respondent).

flaggedAt.description: When the respondent flagged the field.

path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the flagged field within the response.

flagKind.description: Closed taxonomy of respondent self-flag reasons. Extension via the envelope-level extensions block; flagKind itself is a closed enum.

note.description: Optional respondent-authored note explaining the flag. Free text; class inheritance follows the flagged field's accessControl.class when resolvable.

itemKey.description: Optional stable Formspec item key when the path maps directly to one.

attachment_id.description: Stable logical attachment identifier within the current response and origin-layer scope.

slot_path.description: Formspec response path or evidence slot where the attachment is bound.

media_type.description: RFC 6838 media type of the attachment bytes.

byte_length.description: Exact attachment byte length before any adapter encryption, export wrapping, or transport encoding.

attachment_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the exact attachment bytes before any adapter encryption, export wrapping, or transport encoding.

payload_content_hash.description: Hash of the payload bytes as carried by the selected integrity or export profile. For a Trellis-wrapped profile this equals EventPayload.content_hash and PayloadExternal.content_hash; base Formspec attachment lifecycle meaning comes from attachment_id, slot_path, attachment_sha256, and prior_binding_hash.

prior_binding_hash.description: Prior attachment-binding event hash for replacement, or null for first bind.

PrivacyTier.description: Disclosure tier describing how linkable or revealed the subject identity is for the actor or attestation at this event boundary.

errors.description: Count of error-severity validation findings at the event boundary.

warnings.description: Count of warning-severity validation findings at the event boundary.

infos.description: Count of info-severity validation findings at the event boundary.

results.description: Optional detailed ValidationResult snapshot captured alongside the summary counts.

actionId.description: The Action.id from the Response Actions document this invocation references. Mirrors the Action.id pattern published in response-actions.schema.json.

invocationId.description: Unique invocation identifier. Stable across replays of the same invocation. ASCII-printable per the pattern; deterministic UTF-8 encoding for hash-chain inclusion.

attempt.description: 1 on first attempt; 2 on retry-once. Identifies the attempt within an invocation.

terminal.description: Terminal state of the invocation, restricted to the values the four published action.* event kinds emit. action.invoked carries no terminal. action.failed uses failed; action.deferred uses deferred; action.replayed uses replayed. The completed lifecycle moment is covered by response.completed; the blocked terminal manifests via action.failed with a causeRef discriminator.

effectIndex.description: Zero-based index of the EffectRequest in the Action.effects array. Present on action.failed and action.deferred when an effect is the proximate cause.

causeRef.description: Reference to a structured failure or deferral cause owned by the runtime. ASCII-printable per the pattern; deterministic UTF-8 encoding for hash-chain inclusion. The Ledger does not interpret the semantic content.

replayTokenRef.description: Reference to the runtime's replay token. Present on action.deferred. Invocation-scoped: MUST NOT be used to express cross-case or cross-response continuation. ASCII-printable; deterministic UTF-8 encoding.

priorInvocationRef.description: Reference to the prior invocation this event continues. Present on action.replayed. Invocation-lineage scope only; this is not a case continuation handle, response continuation, or session reference.

ActionEventPayload.description: Payload bound to action.invoked / action.failed / action.deferred / action.replayed. The Ledger stores this payload verbatim; it does not interpret the semantic content of opaque *Ref fields, but their byte encoding is constrained so canonical event hashing is deterministic across deployments.

DidString.description: Decentralized identifier string in DID syntax.

HashString.description: Algorithm-prefixed digest or integrity token, such as 'sha256:...'.

Extensions.description: Implementation-specific extension data. Keys must be namespaced with an 'x-' prefix.
